scenario: A regulated claims workflow has deterministic validation steps, one ambiguous classification step, and a payment action.
decision: Choose workflow versus autonomous-agent boundaries and place the approval gate.
must_evidence: state and failure transitions are defined
trap: Making the whole process autonomous because one step needs an LLM.

scenario: Three specialist agents exchange tasks and sometimes hand work back indefinitely.
decision: Design the message contract and termination semantics.
must_evidence: strictly decreasing hop or cost budget
trap: Relying on a prompt asking agents not to loop.

scenario: A report-publishing tool times out after the remote service may already have committed the write.
must_evidence: bounded retry only for transient failures
trap: Blindly retrying a side effect.

scenario: A tool returns malformed JSON mixed with prose and an unknown status value.
must_evidence: no side effect from invalid output
trap: Using string extraction to salvage an action.

scenario: An agent improves on a benchmark after prompts were repeatedly edited while viewing its failures.
decision: Determine whether the gain is credible and redesign evaluation.
trap: Calling the repeatedly inspected benchmark an unbiased test set.

scenario: Task success rises while unauthorized-action rate and tail latency also rise.
decision: Make a release decision using multiple gates.
trap: Collapsing incompatible metrics into one flattering average.

scenario: Traffic bursts cause concurrent agent runs to exhaust downstream tool quotas.
trap: Scaling agent replicas without respecting dependency capacity.

scenario: A new agent image passes health checks but produces worse decisions.
trap: Treating liveness as proof of answer quality.

scenario: A long conversation drops a consent revocation from the context window.
decision: Select a memory design that preserves policy state.
must_evidence: consent stored as explicit authoritative state
retrieval filtered by identity and validity
trap: Depending on rolling chat history for durable authorization.

scenario: A planner repeatedly decomposes a task without making progress.
trap: Increasing token limits as the only remedy.

scenario: A user asks for a confidential policy they cannot access; relevant embeddings exist in the shared index.
trap: Ranking globally and hiding the document only after generation.

scenario: New policy documents arrive continuously and may supersede older versions.
decision: Design ingestion quality and freshness controls.
trap: Appending chunks without supersession semantics.

scenario: A team needs guardrails, model serving, agent components, and optimized high-throughput inference.
decision: Map NVIDIA platform components to responsibilities.
must_evidence: NeMo Guardrails for programmable conversational rails
Agent Toolkit for profiling/optimizing agent workflows
trap: Claiming one NVIDIA component performs every layer.

scenario: A multimodal pipeline meets functional requirements but misses latency targets.
trap: Quantizing immediately without a baseline or quality gate.

scenario: Users report intermittent failures, but average latency is normal.
trap: Using only average latency and uncorrelated logs.

scenario: A retrieval provider outage causes agents to fabricate unsupported answers.
decision: Specify degraded operation and incident response.
trap: Silently answering from model memory when citations are required.

scenario: A retrieved document tells the agent to ignore policy and invoke an administrative tool.
trap: Asking the model to decide whether the malicious instruction is authorized.

scenario: An agent produces disparate approval rates across protected groups.
trap: Declaring fairness from aggregate accuracy.

scenario: An operator sees an approval dialog saying only 'Allow action?'.
trap: Using vague consent that cannot support an informed decision.

scenario: A high-impact action is approved, but its inputs change before execution.
decision: Bind approval to the executed action.
must_evidence: approval covers canonical parameters and version/hash
execution and approver share audit correlation
trap: Treating approval as a reusable global permission.
